questions.text: Given Moor's actual architecture, existing automation, explicit authority boundaries, generators, executors, cognition machinery, child-manufacturing capabilities, retention systems, and owner-observation needs: what is the most efficient and leveraged way to create: (1) a parallel governed bootstrap fleet; (2) task-specific practice environments; (3) inside and outside Funnel-on-Funnel execution; (4) a minimal truthful owner observatory; while preserving authority, detachment, verification, historical integrity, and Less is Moor? [Phase-2 question, commission verbatim]
OWNER SIDE — what work should be parallelized first? Determine from the commission text; the commission names a first bootstrap target unless the Funnel derives a stronger one.
OWNER SIDE — what must the owner see at a glance in the observatory? Determine from the commission's default-screen specification.
OWNER SIDE — which controls are genuinely necessary in the observatory? Determine from the commission's controls specification.
OWNER SIDE — which information deserves interruption, and which can remain drill-down? The commission defines an owner inbox but not thresholds.
OWNER SIDE — what do 'inside' and 'outside' mean for practice environments? Determine from the commission's inside/outside sections.
OWNER SIDE — what kinds of children remain managed, and when should a child detach? The commission defines visibility rules; detach timing is open.
OWNER SIDE — what must be retained after a training run, and what must never be retained?
OWNER SIDE — what level of failure should surface immediately, and what amount of activity is too much to present?
OWNER SIDE — what does success mean for momentum? Determine from the commission's momentum and proofs sections.
MAKER SIDE — which existing mechanisms already support bounded parallel work? Answer against the evidence package; classify each REQUIRED/EXISTING/DERIVED/OPTIONAL/UNKNOWN.
MAKER SIDE — which current machines can serve as task environments? Answer against the evidence; dormant machines must not be assumed available.
MAKER SIDE — what is the smallest common practice contract? Derive from the commission's practice-environment declaration list and the learning test.
MAKER SIDE — which practice environments should live inside Moor, and which should be disposable outside laboratories? Give the deciding criterion from evidence.
MAKER SIDE — which outputs can safely return from practice environments (inside and outside)? Give the return paths from evidence.
MAKER SIDE — what evidence distinguishes learning from logging? Apply the commission's learning test and the Epistemic Law.
MAKER SIDE — what events already exist for truthful observability? Enumerate from the evidence package.
MAKER SIDE — what minimum new events are actually required for the fleet, practice, and observatory? Preserve UNKNOWN; no manufactured certainty.
MAKER SIDE — how is central coordination kept from becoming a bottleneck, given the daemon must stay orchestration-only?
MAKER SIDE — how is Muse kept from being flooded with fleet-wide context?
MAKER SIDE — how is child isolation preserved while showing owner-relevant truth for attached and detached children?
MAKER SIDE — how is the UI projection kept read-only by default, with controls that cannot bypass governance?
MAKER SIDE — how should completed work launch the next bounded wave without creating an authority leak?
test owner q

O1: RANK TIER NAMES. The Funnel derived Moor-native working names: UNRATED / QUALIFIED / PROVEN / SENIOR / SENIOR-OPERATIONAL (military analogy documented as analogy only). Options: (a) keep Moor-native names; (able) use military-analog names (Private..Sergeant Major); (c) owner renames later. Provisional answer: (a) — the commission says 'The Funnel may choose an existing Moor-native name or retain the rank analogy'; the Funnel chose Moor-native. The owner can rename at any time; names confer nothing.
M1: How is SOP-before-task made mechanically load-bearing (not advisory)?
M2: What structurally prevents rank from becoming authority?
M3: How is the closure predicate computed, and what makes 'done' un-utterable?
M4: How are two simultaneous successors structurally prevented?
M5: What makes the mission record durable (not coordinator context)?
M6: What is the truthful relation between base Funnel proof depth and machine rank?
M7: Why these six branches and not others?
M8: Why no echelons below branch, and when would they appear?

P-O1: PROVISIONAL working answer for O1 (rank tier names). The owner's commission states: 'The Funnel may choose an existing Moor-native name or retain the rank analogy.' The Funnel chose Moor-native working names: UNRATED / QUALIFIED / PROVEN / SENIOR / SENIOR-OPERATIONAL. This provisional stands until the owner overrides; names confer nothing and the owner may rename at any time.

P-O2: PROVISIONAL working answer for O2 (command visibility depth). The owner's commission specifies the exact MOOR COMMAND fields (missions with commander/deputy/stage/status/SOP/authority/blockers/owner-judgment/verification; units; machines; SOPs) and orders 'Keep the default view simple. Drill down for detail.' Build to that spec; the owner adjusts on seeing it.

P-O3: PROVISIONAL working answer for O3 (time-in-rank weighting). The owner's commission states: 'Implement time-in-rank only if the Funnel determines it is useful.' The Funnel determined: timestamps on qualification records now; full weighting deferred until a governance need is demonstrated. Time-in-rank never manufactures truth or authority.

P-O4: PROVISIONAL working answer for O4 (C1/C2 conflicts). Both remain open owner decisions, inventoried as governance gaps, explicitly out of scope for this commission. No action taken; the chain-of-command machinery does not depend on their resolution.

questions.text: Given Moor's actual missions, ranks, branches, qualifications, SOPs, recurring duties, capabilities, automation, practice environments, authority boundaries, and command-continuity machinery: what durable jobs should exist so recurring responsibilities can be assigned to qualified machines, governed by the correct SOP bundle, automated where bounded, monitored continuously, succeeded safely, and verified independently without turning jobs into authority?

OWNER-JUDGMENT O1: Three cron paths (funnel-bulletproof-evergreen 4h, funnel-meaning-siphon 6h, funnel-blueprint-compound 12h) form a closed self-improvement loop with no owner, no quoted authorization, and no verification. The Funnel-derived job taxonomy deliberately does NOT launder them into a job. Should they be (a) goal-owned with verification added, (b) parked/disabled until classified, or (c) left running as-is? Left OPEN for Sebastian.
MAKER M1: Which automation triggers from the commission's candidate list actually belong to derived jobs, based on evidence of real recurring duties?
MAKER M2: What SOP bundle does each derived job require, resolved from the actual SOP inventory?
MAKER M3: Single-holder vs multi-holder for each derived job, based on concurrency evidence?
MAKER M4: For each derived job's duties: what part is automatable, what part requires judgment, what part requires owner authority?
MAKER M5: How does succession differ between standing jobs and mission-scoped jobs, using existing machinery?

PLAN REVIEW: does the derived 7-stage plan satisfy — (a) no corporate HR system (jobs continuity-tested, hypotheses rejected with reasons); (b) no duplicated rank/command/SOP/authority (composition only); (c) jobs structurally cannot grant authority; (d) no invisible automation left unowned or silently assigned; (e) all JOB≠ distinctions preserved; (f) proofs/adversarial executable for real?

Given Moor's actual memory, knowledge, provenance, chronology, supersession, retrieval, cognition, and verification machinery (evidence: funnel-docs/moor-knowledge-remind/evidence/evidence-package.md): what is already sufficient for a truthful Knowledge Map; what is already sufficient for backward and forward memory; and what, if anything, is missing for Moor to recognize that stored knowledge has become relevant to the current semantic state and remind Muse or the Funnel without flooding context or creating authority?

OWNER SIDE (options-first, provisional per D3): which Knowledge Map views and reminder behaviors does the owner need? Candidate views: what Moor knows / thinks / can do / has done / does not know / why it believes something / what changed / what depends on something / what Moor should remember right now. Candidate reminder behaviors: small bounded reminders with provenance+status; no auto-admission; no flooding.

MAKER-1 retrieval reality: what knowledge is reachable now; what requires exact IDs; what retrieval is semantic vs chronological vs provenance vs dependency vs supersession; what stores have no live callers; what memories are never queried; which cognition paths forget to consult memory. Evidence: funnel-docs/moor-knowledge-remind/evidence/evidence-package.md and inventory-A/B/C.

MAKER-2 remind design: where does semantic state exist before Muse is invoked; where can relevance be computed without widening authority; what should trigger a reminder vs what must never trigger automatically; what causes reminder storms and how are they suppressed; how do reminders go stale; what happens on remembered-vs-current evidence conflict; how is UNKNOWN handled. Evidence: funnel-docs/moor-knowledge-remind/evidence/evidence-package.md and inventory-A/B/C.

D7: v44 #2 (owner side: options-first, open text never load-bearing, never stall on open-ended questions) vs new framing (deep bounded semantic answers from Muse). Determine from owner intent and existing architecture whether the correct composition is the two-lane split — OWNER SIDE: options-first / never stalled by open text / open text not load-bearing; MAKER SIDE: bounded semantic response / implementation-depth framing / evidence-bearing answer / bounce if incomplete — or another composition that better fits established law. Constraint: do not manufacture v45; preserve the stronger proven rule where rules overlap.
